title: The empty refund answers
scenario: A shop's refund checker reads an order and the refund policy, then returns 'eligible' or 'not eligible' with a one-line reason. It runs on an OpenAI reasoning model. About 8% of responses come back with no visible answer. The monthly bill is also higher than planned. Most requests are simple: unused items returned within 30 days. You review the request settings, the prompt and one log line (exhibit).
exhibit:
request:
  reasoning.effort: xhigh
  max_output_tokens: 500

instructions:
  Think step by step. Write out your full reasoning,
  then give the decision and a one-line reason.

log (failed request):
  status: incomplete
  incomplete_details.reason: max_output_tokens
  usage.output_tokens: 500
  usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens: 500
  visible text: (none)

questions.prompt: Why do some responses have no visible answer?

options.text: The model refused the request for safety reasons.
options.explanation: A refusal would not show reason max_output_tokens. The log says the output cap was hit.

options.text: Reasoning used the whole 500-token cap before any answer text was written.
options.explanation: Right. Reasoning tokens count toward max_output_tokens. The OpenAI docs say the cap can be reached before any visible output.

options.text: The order text was too long and pushed the answer out of the model's context window.
options.explanation: The log points at the output cap, not the context window: 500 of 500 output tokens were reasoning.

options.text: Streaming was off, so the answer was lost in transit.
options.explanation: Streaming changes when you receive tokens, not whether they are generated.

questions.prompt: What should the team change about the output cap and effort?

options.text: Lower max_output_tokens to 200 to force shorter reasoning.
options.explanation: A smaller cap makes the failure more common. It cuts output; it does not make the model reason less.

options.text: Keep xhigh effort and add 'keep your reasoning under 400 tokens' to the prompt.
options.explanation: Prompt wording is soft guidance, not a limit. xhigh also suits deep, long tasks, which this is not.

options.text: Size the cap for reasoning plus answer, and lower the effort for this task.
options.explanation: Right. The cap must fit reasoning and answer; the OpenAI docs suggest reserving at least 25,000 tokens when you start. Lower effort cuts reasoning and cost.

options.text: Turn on streaming so partial reasoning reaches the user.
options.explanation: Reasoning tokens are not visible via the API, so there is nothing to stream to the user.

questions.prompt: What should happen to the line 'Think step by step. Write out your full reasoning'?

options.text: Keep it, because written-out reasoning makes every refund decision auditable later.
options.explanation: It sounds safe, but it adds visible output tokens on top of hidden reasoning. If you need a trail, ask for the short one-line reason you already have.

options.text: Move it to the end of the prompt so the model sees it last.
options.explanation: Position does not fix the problem. The instruction itself is the issue for a reasoning model.

options.text: Repeat it twice so the model reasons more carefully.
options.explanation: More reasoning is the opposite of what this task needs, and the OpenAI docs advise against chain-of-thought prompts here.

options.text: Remove it, because the model reasons internally and the docs advise against such prompts.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say such prompts are unnecessary and can sometimes hinder performance.

questions.prompt: Most refund checks are simple; a few are real disputes. Which design fits the vendor guidance best?

options.text: Use max effort for every request, to be safe.
options.explanation: The OpenAI docs say to use xhigh only when evals show a clear benefit that justifies the extra latency and cost. Max is above that.

options.text: Low effort for routine checks, higher for disputes, one test set for both.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI maps low effort to support-style workflows and high effort to hard reasoning. Both vendors say to measure the change.

options.text: Turn reasoning off everywhere and add 'think step by step' to the prompt instead.
options.explanation: That swaps a tuned setting for a prompt trick. The OpenAI docs advise against chain-of-thought prompts on reasoning models.

options.text: Send every request twice and keep the longer answer.
options.explanation: That doubles cost, and a longer answer is not a more correct one.
